title: Corpus documents and frozen partitions
description: The source units and data roles used before fitting a learned tokenizer or model.

terms.definition: A collection of source documents from which training, validation, and test data are assigned.
A complete source text assigned to one role, with its start and end preserved during tokenization and window creation.
Documents used to fit learned tokenizer rules and model weights.
Documents outside fitting that guide choices among training-fitted systems or saved model states.
Documents reserved for reporting after fitting and selection are complete; using their result to choose again makes them part of selection.
An assignment that covers every corpus document and gives no document to different roles; manifest lists also need checks for repeated positions and order.
Documents kept outside fitting for validation or test assessment; they may supply evaluation statistics without fitting counts or gradients.
A breach of the intended separation between fitting and assessment, as when overlapping excerpts from one source occupy training and a holdout.
A label joining documents with known related source content, such as translations of one scene, so they stay in one role.
The tokenizer learned in Chapter 3 using pair counts from training documents only, with no pair counted across a document boundary; frozen rules can later encode holdout text.
